claim_text: Genetic variants identified in the present study may be insufficient to promote early carotid atherosclerosis.

Mitochondria play a role in remodeling lace plant leaves during programmed cell death by regulating perforation formation through modulation of calcium channels and activation of specific proteases that degrade cellular structures.
A proposed entity termed "aquagenic maladies" could be a pediatric form of aquagenic urticaria.

In patients undergoing emergency laparotomy, nutritional deficiencies and lack of adequate immunomodulatory support significantly contribute to high mortality rates, particularly among patients older than 70 years.
Among HMO women, tailored text messages were found to be as effective as tailored print communications in increasing mammography use.
Correction for reporting heterogeneity using anchoring vignettes is not a necessary tool for proper management of sleep- and energy-related problems among Japanese adults.
In patients with strabismus amblyopia, visual acuity is significantly underestimated when assessed with the Landolt C chart compared with the Snellen E chart.
The study leaves unresolved why the tailored print intervention was not more powerful.

Among HMO women targeted for mammography screening interventions, the intervention effects were most pronounced after the first intervention. Compared with usual care, telephone counseling appeared particularly effective at promoting change among nonadherent women, the group for whom the intervention was developed. These results suggest that telephone counseling, rather than tailored print, may be the preferred first-line intervention for getting nonadherent women on schedule for mammography screening.
This report states that, for the first time, cyclosporin A (CsA) was shown to be feasible for use in a whole-plant system.
Double-balloon enteroscopy appears to be as safe and effective when performed in a community setting as in a tertiary referral center, with comparable yield, efficacy, and complication rates.

In the long-term study, the abdominal approach had a significantly better continence score, about 2-fold better than the transanal pull-through, whereas stool pattern and enterocolitis scores were somewhat better in the TERPT group; these mixed findings raise an important issue for the current surgical management of Hirschsprung disease, and more cases are needed before a definitive conclusion can be drawn.
Additional interventions will be needed to maintain women's adherence to mammography.

Chile's traffic law reform mainly focused on increasing penalties for traffic violations rather than pushing for police enforcement.

Findings suggest that for traffic law reforms to reduce traffic fatality and injury rates, changes in police enforcement practices are required.
Therapeutic anticoagulation in trauma patients has been shown to significantly reduce the risk of deep vein thrombosis without increasing mortality, making it a safe practice for selected patients.
In infants, syncope during bathing is attributed to water-induced vasodilation and hypovolemia, which can lead to transient circulatory collapse.

Mutations that cause low HDL-C levels promote increased carotid intima-media thickness, particularly in the presence of hypertension.

Emergency medicine residents in programs with emergency ultrasound fellowships performed more ultrasound scans overall and used bedside ultrasound for more advanced applications.
Double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) shows slightly higher complication rates in the community setting because less experienced staff perform the procedure there.
The study's MeSH terms are mammography screening, telephone counseling, tailored print communications, and barriers.

Retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy in a porcine model is feasible and could be very useful for teaching and practicing retroperitoneoscopy.

Unvaccinated seniors exhibit distinct patterns based on their beliefs and fears regarding the effectiveness and side effects of the influenza vaccine.
Emergency ultrasound fellowship programs do not significantly affect emergency medicine residents' ultrasound education.

Prospective studies are needed in sub-Saharan African populations to establish the potential value of resting heart rate in cardiovascular risk assessment.
Emergency ultrasound fellowship programs had a positive impact on emergency medicine residents' ultrasound educational experiences.

In palliative care patients with breathlessness, opioid patient-controlled therapy reportedly significantly reduces breathlessness through traditional opioid receptor activation plus modulation of serotonin and norepinephrine levels; this proposed dual-action mechanism is described as providing more comprehensive symptom reduction and improving patient comfort.

Higher MCVs and AST/ALT ratios in alcoholic steatohepatitis reflect the severity of underlying liver disease and do not differentiate nonalcoholic steatohepatitis from alcoholic steatohepatitis; instead, these biomarkers might be useful for selecting patients for liver biopsy and for targeting therapy.
Among unvaccinated seniors, findings suggest that cluster analyses may be useful for identifying groups for targeted health messages.
In terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents, approximately 70% of arriving casualties will need immediate medical attention.

Elevated resting heart rate is relevant to cardiovascular risk because it is linked to increased risk of cardiovascular disease through greater arterial stiffness and endothelial dysfunction; studies suggest that resting heart rate above 85 beats per minute is associated with enhanced arterial stiffness and impaired endothelial function, which contribute to cardiovascular morbidity.

In pediatric liver transplantation, short- and long-term outcomes after living-related transplantation (LRT) and split-liver transplantation (SLT) do not differ significantly; therefore, in countries where cadaveric organs are available, SLT is the first-line therapy to avoid donor risk from LRT.

In children with malignancy and acute respiratory distress syndrome, peak inspiratory pressure, PEEP, and ventilation index values could distinguish survivors from nonsurvivors by day 3, and this prognostic information may assist in early application of supportive nonconventional therapies.

Hospital preparedness for terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents should focus on a dynamic assessment model that predicts the exact number of severe cases likely to require intensive care based on historical data from similar incidents.
In children with malignancy and ARDS, the presence of leukemic blast cells in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid on admission is a significant predictor of poor prognosis.
The effectiveness of epidural analgesia during labor varies significantly among different ethnic groups, indicating that cultural factors play a critical role in its successful implementation.
A virtual reality-based simulation has been developed and validated for teaching and practicing retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy.

Studies suggest that implementing comprehensive preoperative nutritional assessment and perioperative immunomodulation in patients undergoing emergency laparotomy can markedly reduce 30-day mortality rates to around 10%.

In pediatric liver transplantation, living-related transplantation (LRT) remains useful for urgent cases when a cadaveric graft cannot be found in time or when precise timing of transplantation is critical.

Among infants discharged from the NICU, the most disadvantaged families are least likely to have protective health behaviors in place to reduce secondhand smoke exposure (SHSe) and therefore are at highest risk for tobacco exposure and subsequent tobacco-related health disparities; innovative SHSe interventions are needed for this vulnerable population.
Only 20% of arriving casualties will require immediate medical treatment.

Currently available nomograms used to predict BCR accurately predict PCSM and other more clinically relevant endpoints, and they generally predict PCSM with greater accuracy than they predict BCR.

Hospital preparedness for terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents can be better defined by a fixed number of casualties rather than by a percentile of bed capacity, and implementing this approach may improve the utilization of national emergency health resources during both the preparation phase and real time response.

An audit found that implementation of labor analgesia was quick, successful, and safe; however, one cluster of women had a suboptimal response to epidural analgesia and requires further study, and overall pregnant women's adherence to labor analgesia was satisfactory.

Older people with a history of amblyopia who develop visual loss in the previously normal fellow eye can experience recovery of visual function in the amblyopic eye over time, and this improvement appears to be sustained.
Sleep disorders are common in the general adult population of Japan.
HER2 immunoreactivity might have limited prognostic value in advanced urothelial carcinoma patients receiving adjuvant M-VEC chemotherapy.

Visceral adipose tissue area measurement at a single CT slice 3 cm above the lower margin of the L3 vertebra is feasible, can reflect interval changes in visceral adipose tissue volume and body weight, and should be selected at this location because it best reflects those changes.

Halofantrine is primarily associated with cardiovascular side effects rather than ototoxicity; although studies have shown that halofantrine can affect auditory structures under certain conditions, its main risk is cardiac toxicity, especially when halofantrine is administered in high doses or over extended periods.
Visual loss due to amblyopia is permanent unless amblyopia is treated with early intervention during childhood.
HER2 immunoreactivity provides definitive prognostic value for patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma receiving adjuvant M-VEC chemotherapy.
In patients aged 80 or older with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, conservative treatment yields similar outcomes to aneurysm repair.
Visceral adipose tissue area measurement at a single level 3 cm below the lower margin of the L3 vertebra is feasible and can reflect changes in visceral adipose tissue volume and body weight.
In fractures of the talar neck (astragalus), a positive Hawkins sign rules out avascular necrosis of the fractured talus, but absence of the Hawkins sign does not confirm avascular necrosis.

Effective undergraduate surgical education can be provided in many specialty settings, so removing the requirement for a general surgery rotation in the clerkship may allow more effective use of available educational opportunities.
This study's results cast doubt on whether hyperbaric oxygenation therapy reduces mortality and morbidity when used as adjuvant therapy for necrotizing fasciitis.

Mandatory general surgery rotations are necessary in the surgical clerkship because they provide foundational skills for all surgical subspecialties, including critical procedural competencies unique to general surgery that cannot be replicated elsewhere during the clerkship.

In patients aged 80 or older with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, repair of the ruptured aneurysm was associated with a better prognosis than conservative treatment; therefore, definitive surgery should not be withheld in this elderly population.
Before recommending removal of the general surgery requirement to other institutions, a careful analysis of local programs and facilities is necessary.
Well differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma is considered an early-stage cancer because it has a lower incidence of fibrous capsule formation and lacks portal vein invasion.
The findings showed that acupuncture at voice-related acupoints could improve vocal function and promote healing of vocal fold lesions.
Nomograms designed to predict biochemical recurrence perform poorly compared with other tools when used to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality and other clinically relevant endpoints.

Patient adherence to follow-up recommendations for abnormal Papanicolaou smears is significantly higher when genetic counseling is integrated into the follow-up protocol.

The real-time PCR approach demonstrated limited effectiveness for pollen identification and quantification, particularly in complex mixtures, and further studies are necessary to refine the real-time PCR approach.

Analyses found that structural characteristics of a general practice were not associated with uptake of a new IT facility, but use of the facility may have been influenced by post-graduate education in the relevant clinical condition.

In fractures of the neck of the astragalus, a negative Hawkins sign is predictive of avascular necrosis.
The real-time PCR approach showed promising results for pollen identification and quantification, including when analyzing mixed-pollen samples.

Further studies should examine physicians' perception of the utility of prompts for family history risk.
For this diabetes IT system, practice nurse use was critical for spreading uptake beyond the initial general practitioner enthusiasts and for sustaining and increasing use in subsequent years.

Advanced surface ablation (ASA) and sub-Bowman's keratomileusis (SBK) both demonstrate superior wound healing characteristics compared with conventional LASIK and significantly reduce the risk of postoperative corneal ectasia.
Compared with non-diabetic patients, FDG-PET accuracy in cervical cancer patients with mild to moderate diabetes mellitus was not significantly reduced.

Among patients undergoing pelvic exenteration for locally recurrent rectal cancer, prior radiotherapy for the primary rectal cancer is associated with worse oncologic outcomes than no prior radiotherapy.

Sub-Bowman's keratomileusis (SBK) has a higher incidence of interface-related complications than advanced surface ablation (ASA) because of SBK's distinct wound healing profile.
Most disadvantages related to wound healing still remain after sub-Bowman's keratomileusis (SBK) and advanced surface ablation (ASA).

Structural characteristics of a general practice, including the number of GPs and staff training status, significantly affect uptake of new IT facilities, indicating a direct relationship between these factors and IT adoption rate in primary care.
Practicing surgeons rely on visual inspection and palpation to detect early lymphedema with high accuracy.

In colorectal cancer with synchronous liver metastases, sequential management (SM) was associated with a longer delay and increased use of chemotherapy between procedures, and the response suggests that stricter surgical selection of SM patients may explain the higher disease-free survival after synchronous liver metastasis resection.
Halofantrine has mild to moderate pathological effects on cochlear histology and can be considered an ototoxic drug.

An increase of 5% in circumference measurements identified the most potential lymphedema cases compared with an academic trial.

Transgastric endoscopic splenectomy has been successfully performed in human clinical trials with minimal postoperative recovery time.
